categories.description: Unit selection, status reports and journal excerpts.
categories.name: Arguments

options.summary: Use the current user’s service manager
options.detail: Selects units managed for the calling user.

options.summary: Use the system service manager
options.detail: This is the default manager.

options.summary: Write output without a pager
Applies to table legends only
options.detail: The status report has no table legend. Its unit heading and journal excerpt remain visible.

options.summary: Show status text at full width
options.detail: Preserve long unit names, descriptions, process tree entries and journal messages. Short spelling: -l.

options.summary: Show status for all units in memory
options.detail: With no operands or unit filters, print the manager overview followed by unit reports. A named unit still selects that unit. Short spelling: -a.

options.summary: Show status for matching unit types
options.detail: With no operand or a unit glob, select types such as service,timer. An explicit unit name is looked up directly. Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 require a value after =. Short spelling: -t.

options.summary: Show status for units in selected states

bare.reason: This is a text/selector grammar, not an unsuffixed scalar measurement

forms.grammar: Comma-separated load, active or substate names, such as loaded, active, inactive, failed or running; meanings and available substates depend on unit type. help requests the state-name list.

when_absent.meaning: Use the selected subcommand's normal state filtering.

options.detail: Use --state=failed without a unit name to inspect failed units. Explicit unit names bypass this filter. Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 require a value after =.

options.summary: Applies to listing symbols only
options.detail: The unit status heading and process tree keep their usual formatting.
The default is 10 per unit. Use --lines=0 to hide the journal excerpt while keeping the status report. Short spelling: -n.
options.summary: Set the number of recent journal entries

options.summary: Query a remote system manager
options.detail: Connect over SSH. Use [USER@]HOST[:PORT][/CONTAINER]. Enclose an IPv6 address in brackets. Remote transport requires system scope. Also spelled -H.

options.summary: Query a remote system manager
options.detail: Connect over SSH. Use [USER@]HOST[:PORT][/CONTAINER]. Enclose an IPv6 address in brackets. Remote transport requires system scope. Also spelled --host=.

options.summary: Query a local container manager
options.detail: Use a container name or USER@MACHINE. With --user, USER@.host selects a user manager on this host. Also spelled -M.

options.summary: Query a local container manager
options.detail: Use a container name or USER@MACHINE. With --user, USER@.host selects a user manager on this host. Also spelled --machine=.

options.summary: Connect to the manager in a capsule
options.detail: Supply a capsule name. The capsule provides its own service manager. Available in Ubuntu 26.04 and upstream 262. Ubuntu 24.04 lacks this option. Also spelled -C.

options.summary: Connect to the manager in a capsule
